about: What the loading card shows after an update (#745): per release, newest first, up to five short player-facing lines. Written by tools/release/whats-new.mjs.

lines: Outdoor skies follow the clock, with stars at night.
Read, answer and close your bug reports on the website too, under Community's Support.
Drag a machine you've set down to slide it along the floor, right up next to another.
Eight more reactions to pick from: 👏 😊 🤔 😍 🔥 👀 😅 and 💯.
What's new in the Menu shows every version, with ‹ › or the arrow keys to step through them.
Walk onto a crack or Manhole rug on an upper floor of your house and you drop to the floor below.
Decoration Mode scrolls into the back yard, so you can pick up and move what lies there.
Things dragged from your pack land where you let go in your back yard.
The Bureaucratic Hall has its eight waiting chairs, and you stand on its floor again.
Prices read the number then ₡ everywhere: shops, vendors, storage, mail and auctions.
A window left open on a laptop that went to sleep no longer takes your character back when it wakes.
A machine that can't go down because you stand too close to the others now says so.
Something that ended up under the house floor comes back up onto it.
Visiting Stones on East Spice and four other streets stand at their street's end again.
A long description in an item's menu no longer squeezes its actions into a few rows.
Archimedes Acres's Group Hall has its own street for its group's members.
Drinks at the Pot Luck Day feast offer Drink, and drinking them works.
On a computer, only things in reach glow under the mouse, as in Glitch.
Progress Way's camera pan to the Street Spirit works, as in Glitch.
The Map's home card has House and Tower buttons beside Home.
Doors on the street map show what they are: a dino, a portal or a door.
The energy and mood rings change colour as they empty, as Glitch's gauges did.
Apple a Day gives its +5 energy when it ends, and every buff's end effect lands.
Croaking Piggies keep their own minute instead of all croaking as you arrive.
The teleporters on Ain't That Dry, Chiti Tiga and Harrisa Hara work again.
The secret passage behind the trunk in Koulato Cluster takes you to Ruta Asuncion again.
Open water and deep shafts no longer stop you on an invisible floor: you sink to the bottom.
Notes played on Piano Party's keys and stars are heard by everyone on the street.
Players' names are coloured in chat and in speech bubbles, one colour each.
Walking up to your house or pointing at it no longer makes the world blink out or go blank.
The glow around Helga and other vendors stays on their body through every animation.
Giant Icons can be placed at home, and visitors can Ruminate, Revere, Reflect and Tithe.
One click or tap on a garden plot does its job: harvest, hoe, water or fertilize.
A group's administrator can rename the group and change its description.
Coming back to the game from another page reconnects it, so chat and shared actions work again.
On a computer, things in reach glow, as in Glitch, instead of a label following you.
Only the owner, key holders and visitors let in can see inside a house and its back yard, as in Glitch.
Those inside can dig a back yard's Dirt Piles and work its Peat Bogs, shared with the owner.
When the owner logs off, visitors without a key are walked out to the front door.
The Game Show ticket's spinning wheel draws in front of barnacles.
Camera Mode at your own home can snap the whole house, Tower or home street, every floor stacked.
On a computer, sound keeps playing when you switch tabs, with a setting to choose.
Playing a musicblock for someone shows its bubble over them and gives them the block and notes.
Wall pieces go as high as Glitch allowed.
A visitor sees every Dirt Pile, Peat Bog and Patch in a friend's back yard.
Expand opens Glitch's dialog: what the next segment costs, what you have, and a button to use them.
Visitors see the owner's own house style.
A dead connection is found in seconds and says "Reconnecting...".
A Subway ticket plays the teleport chime, and stations play their region's music.
A gem found while mining shows in the activity log.
Butterflies and Batterflies wander their whole street at random, and everyone sees them in the same place.
Your first shrine donation offers Respect for the Beginnings again.
Show the way never sends you through a locked door you have no key for.
Music and sounds pause while you are in another app or tab, and pick up where they left off.
Firebog street spirits' flames flicker and their vines sway.
A room holds any number of furniture pieces, as in Glitch, and visitors see every one.
Sparkly of Interest shows its count on each step and finishes at 100.
A quest's place link opens the Map on the way into its region, with a Show the way button.
Quest steps read as words, not the quest editor's placeholders.
The Vine Radio: play 6 tunes for the Music Crabs and get a radio for your home street.
Sorted bags show a small badge with what they are sorted for.
The Bookcase can be made again on the Construction Tool.
Machines and the Crafty Bot work on every floor of your house, as in Glitch.
Encyclopedia How do I guides give short answers to questions players asked.
Encyclopedia search finds what each page says, not only its name, and shows what matched.
Street lists: every street with a community garden, a shrine to each Giant, a vendor, a subway and more.
On a phone at home, Decorate, Cultivate and Change Style have their own row under your home's name.
On a phone, your house and Tower floors fill the screen.
In the upright iPhone Home Screen app, the street runs up to the top bar again.
Snaps are taken at full screen size and open in a full-screen viewer with Previous and Next.
Snaps stay private until you make one public; public ones show on your profile.
Piles in your house and on your Tower floors, shelves and tables have no stack limit.
Home street music changes with the street style, as in Glitch.
The Game Show wheel can be spun the moment it appears.
A quiet release: behind-the-scenes work for the game's administrators.
Things you drop, drag or set down in your house show at once instead of after a pause.
Emblems and other one-to-a-stack things pile up on your house floor, shelves and tables.
Things you set on your house or Tower floor are for everyone there again, as in Glitch.
Moving one of your locked things onto the floor unlocks it.
You can move floor stacks along the floor in Decoration Mode.
